rationale:
Quota today: 1 long-form, 3 Shorts, 0 carousels.

**Long-form.** It doesn't need to be a search-demand format. Three of the last 7 long videos already were: First Month (11-13), Pen how-to (11-11) and Foundayo what-to-expect (11-11). So L1 goes to priority action #2 from the playbook: keeping results after stopping, a broad searched question.
- **Different from the 11-04 Stopping video:** that one asked "what happens when you stop". This one asks "how do you keep results", using the long-term evidence on keeping weight off.
- **Fits the rules:** news stays in a one-line hook, the body rests on settled peer-reviewed trial data, and it doesn't hang on any single trial.
- **Skipped:** "Not working" overlaps the Plateau and How Long videos, and plateau long-forms are on the don't-make-more list. It also got a Short on 11-14. NAION had a Short on 11-10 and a long-form on 11-14, so it would repeat inside 30 days. CagriSema's REDEFINE 4 already had a long-form on 10-18, and we have no confirmed new full data. EloraTZP has no tirzepatide-alone arm, so the pipeline ban applies.

**Shorts.** Two of the three are practical moments:
- **S1, pen left out of the fridge:** storage from the label and Instructions for Use, a searched question with no dosing. It points to the Pen long-form.
- **S3, stepping on the scale after stopping:** spin-off of L1.
- **S2, the 13:00 lead:** a calm "what's confirmed?" on the new EloraTZP Phase 2 data. "eloralintide" and "eloratzp" are our best search terms. It must say plainly that the trial was in type 2 diabetes, that it's Phase 2 and that the drug is investigational.

**Not used today:**
- Hair: this week's one hair Short already ran on 11-13.
- Injection site: three recent pieces already.
- Thanksgiving and alcohol: they wait until Nov 18, per the analytics.
- Gray-market, teen and psychiatric case-report angles: caution or low priority.

**Spread:** pillars are life-on-glp1 ×2, get-the-most and research. Topics cover maintenance and behaviour, the device, a pipeline result and self-monitoring, so no body system repeats. Stages: rising ×2, evergreen ×1, emerging ×1.

pieces.topic: Keeping results after stopping tirzepatide (Mounjaro/Zepbound): what the long-term evidence shows about keeping weight off. Regain varies a lot between people. The evidence links ongoing care and structured habits to holding on. Obesity is treated as a chronic condition.
pieces.angle: Drop the ObesityWeek hook. Open with: 'Stopped tirzepatide, or thinking about life after it? Here's what the research shows about keeping results.' By 15 s: on average weight tends to come back after stopping, but how much varies widely, and ongoing care and habits are linked to keeping more of it off. Use the Cleveland Clinic cohort only if the peer-reviewed paper or abstract loads, and then only as one line: 'In one real-world observational study of semaglutide or tirzepatide, people who stopped after 3 to 12 months had lost less to begin with, and 45% of the obesity group held their weight or kept losing over a year. It's observational and covers both drugs.' Otherwise leave it out. Keep all SURMOUNT-4, BMJ and SURMOUNT-1 figures at their exact scope. Retitle to 'Tirzepatide (Mounjaro): Keeping Weight Off After' (49 characters) or 'Tirzepatide (Mounjaro): Can You Keep the Results?' (49 characters). Keep the thumbnail 'KEEP IT OFF?' as planned.
pieces.target_keyword: how to keep weight off after mounjaro
pieces.why: It's priority action #2 and on the double-down list. Stopping is our best recent broad video (6.35% CTR, 309 min by day 10), and ObesityWeek coverage is pushing the same search right now. | fact-check: This is a broad, searched question and the core evidence holds up: SURMOUNT-4 (335 vs 335, +14.0% regain on placebo from week 36 to 88, placebo still 9.9% below baseline), the BMJ 2025 regain meta-analysis, the SURMOUNT-1 off-treatment period in adults with prediabetes, and guidelines that call obesity a chronic disease. Two things need changing. (1) The ObesityWeek hook dates an evergreen video, which breaks the craft rule against 'now', 'new' and conference-dated framing. It also points to the Cleveland Clinic cohort, which I could only trace to newsroom and secondary coverage. That cohort is observational, real-world and covers semaglutide AND tirzepatide. People stopped after 3–12 months having lost only about 8.4% on average, and 27% switched to another medicine within the year. So its '45% held or kept losing' figure (obesity group only) can't be set beside trial figures or credited to tirzepatide alone. (2) 'How to Keep Results' promises a proven method, but the habit evidence only supports 'linked to'. Everything else in the angle (habit hedging, kidney caveat, no stopping, tapering or dosing advice, the case reports left out) is sound.

pieces.topic: Left your tirzepatide pen out of the fridge? What the US label and Instructions for Use say about storage, and what to do if you're unsure.
pieces.angle:
08:00 practical-moment 'Is this normal / is it OK?' Short, tight arm (90–120 words).

- **Sentence 1 (14 words or fewer):** 'Left your tirzepatide pen out of the fridge? Here's what the label says.'
- **By 6 s:** the label's unrefrigerated-storage wording, with its exact temperature and day limits. Copy them from the current Zepbound PI (rev. 28 Aug 2026) and the single-dose pen IFU, each with its own URL. Quote only if the IFU loads.
- **Other label storage lines:** don't freeze, and don't use a pen that has been frozen. Protect it from light, as the label prints it.
- **Scope:** the US single-dose pen. KwikPens and vials have their own leaflets, and UK and Australian packs may differ, so check the leaflet in your box.
- **Untagged line:** if you're not sure whether a pen is still OK, ask your pharmacist before using it.
- **Leave out:** dose amounts, missed-dose talk, travel dates and holiday words.
- **Closing:** the scoped don't-stop/change line, then 'Not personal advice', the prescriber line and the closing line. Exp F is still running, so the Exp F line goes second to last.
- **Post note:** the related-video target is the Pen how-to long video (11-11).
pieces.working_title: Tirzepatide Pen Left Out of the Fridge: OK? #shorts
pieces.why: It's a practical pen moment that people search for. It's fresh (no storage Short yet), and it gives the Pen long-form a feeder.

pieces.topic: EloraTZP (eloralintide + tirzepatide) new Phase 2 data at ObesityWeek: adults with obesity or overweight and type 2 diabetes, 23.3% average weight loss at 48 weeks, A1C down 2.9 points (Lilly-reported)
pieces.angle: Sentence 1: 'EloraTZP, eloralintide plus tirzepatide, in type 2 diabetes: here's what's confirmed.' By 6 s: 'In a Phase 2 trial in adults with obesity or overweight and type 2 diabetes, the top EloraTZP dose averaged 23.3% weight loss at 48 weeks, against 14.8% on tirzepatide 15 mg alone.' Next: 'A1C fell 2.9 points against 2.4.' Credit as 'company-reported, Phase 2, not yet peer-reviewed' (only if no peer-reviewed paper exists; check first). Source: Lilly's primary PR Newswire release, never StockTitan. Leave out 'new' and 'ObesityWeek'. Keep: 'amylin is a second fullness hormone', the per-arm nausea rate if it's published, 'EloraTZP is investigational and isn't approved anywhere', 'ask a prescriber about approved options or a clinical trial'. Keep the closing order as planned. Suggested title: 'EloraTZP vs Tirzepatide in Type 2 Diabetes #shorts'.
pieces.working_title: EloraTZP in Type 2 Diabetes: What's Confirmed? #shorts
pieces.why: It follows up our biggest earner (44% of long-form watch time), and 'eloralintide' and 'eloratzp' are our proven search terms. It also feeds that long video's views back in while its daily minutes are slipping. | fact-check: The figures check out (top dose 23.3% weight loss and 2.9-point A1C drop at 48 weeks, adults with obesity or overweight and type 2 diabetes, Phase 2b NCT06603571, Lilly-reported). But the framing is wrong in two ways. (1) This isn't new ObesityWeek data. The results were first released around 1–2 Oct 2026 (EASD 2026; Lilly release, Healio 2 Oct, Medscape). ObesityWeek was a re-presentation, so calling it 'new' breaks the craft rule against calling older data new. (2) The trial DID have a randomized tirzepatide-alone arm: tirzepatide 15 mg gave 14.8% weight loss and a 2.4-point A1C drop, against 23.3% and 2.9 for the top EloraTZP dose. So the planned 'no tirzepatide-alone comparison' fallback would be false. Also check that the 10-01 'Did EloraTZP Beat Tirzepatide?' long-form isn't about this same trial. If it is, the Short must still add one new fact (for example the A1C result, or the share reaching normal blood sugar if the primary release prints it).

pieces.topic: Stepping on the scale after stopping tirzepatide: why regular self-weighing is linked to keeping weight off in weight-maintenance research, and how to keep it calm and useful
pieces.angle:
20:00 funnel Short and spin-off of L1. It asks one fresh question (self-monitoring), not a re-cut of L1 or the 10-27 hunger Short. Standard arm (135–160 words).

- **Sentence 1:** 'Stopped tirzepatide and scared of the scale?' plus the short answer by 6 s: in weight-maintenance studies, regular self-weighing is linked to keeping more weight off. Cite a peer-reviewed RCT or systematic review, labelled 'linked to'. These weren't tirzepatide trials.
- **New fact:** one SURMOUNT-4 line that matches L1's verified script exactly, plus 'regain varies between people; averages, not predictions'.
- **Untagged tips:** look at the trend, not one day. Share it with your prescriber or care team so problems get caught early.
- **Caveat:** if weighing makes you anxious, or you've had disordered eating, follow your care team's plan instead of tracking numbers. Weight is one health measure among many.
- **Leave out:** guilt, calorie talk, and any stopping or tapering advice.
- **Closing:** the scoped don't-stop/change line ('plan any change with your prescriber'), one GI line, 'Not personal advice', the prescriber line and the closing line. No Exp F line in the 20:00 slot.
- **Post note:** the related-video target is L1 once it's verified live, otherwise the Stopping long video.
pieces.working_title: Tirzepatide Stopped: Should You Keep Weighing? #shorts
pieces.why: Spin-off of L1. It's a practical moment on the rising 'keeping results after stopping' search, and it points viewers to L1 or Stopping through the related-video link.
